nodes.label: Eastern Catholic
nodes.note: The 23 sui iuris churches in communion with Rome — Ukrainian Greek, Maronite, Chaldean, Melkite, Syro-Malabar. Added 2026-08-27 when Canada arrived: ASARB has no category for them, StatCan enumerates nine. Distinct from independent Catholic bodies, which are NOT in communion, and from Eastern Orthodoxy, which is a different communion again.

nodes.label: Independent Catholic
nodes.note: Bodies using Catholic orders and rites outside communion with Rome — Polish National, Old Roman, Liberal Catholic and the small ecumenical Catholic jurisdictions. Distinct from Eastern Catholic churches, which ARE in communion.

nodes.label: Canonical Orthodox
nodes.note: Jurisdictions in communion with the recognised patriarchates.

nodes.label: Old Calendarist
nodes.note: Broke over the 1924 calendar reform; out of communion with the canonical churches.

nodes.label: Other Orthodox jurisdictions
nodes.note: Self-declared autocephalous or independent bodies recognised by nobody. Kept separate rather than folded into canonical, because the distinction is the whole content of these groups' identity.

nodes.label: Oriental Orthodox
nodes.note: The non-Chalcedonian churches — Coptic, Ethiopian, Eritrean, Armenian, Syriac, Malankara. A separate communion from Eastern Orthodoxy since 451, and conflating the two is the commonest error in religion taxonomies.

nodes.label: Continuing Anglican
nodes.note: Bodies that left the Episcopal Church, mostly after 1977 and 2003. A crowded field of small jurisdictions, which is why they get their own node rather than sitting beside the Episcopal Church as peers.

nodes.label: Continental Reformed
nodes.note: Dutch, German and related Reformed churches, as against the Scottish Presbyterian line.

nodes.label: National Baptist conventions
nodes.note: The historically African-American conventions.

nodes.label: Landmark Baptist
nodes.note: The ABA/BMA line, holding to Baptist church succession.

nodes.label: Independent Fundamental Baptist
nodes.note: The separatist fundamentalist associations.

nodes.label: African Methodist
nodes.note: AME, AME Zion, CME and the smaller bodies of the same origin — separated over racial exclusion, not doctrine, which is why they are a branch rather than scattered.

nodes.label: Holiness Methodist
nodes.note: Bodies that left Methodism over the holiness movement, keeping Methodist polity.

nodes.label: United Brethren and Evangelical
nodes.note: The German-speaking American parallel to Methodism; most of it merged into the UMC.

nodes.label: Oneness Pentecostal
nodes.note: Rejects the Trinity and baptises in Jesus' name. The 1916 split is the deepest division inside Pentecostalism and is invisible if these sit among the others.

nodes.label: Charismatic and neo-charismatic
nodes.note: Later movements — Vineyard, Calvary Chapel — outside the classical Pentecostal bodies.

nodes.label: Stone-Campbell Restorationist
nodes.note: Churches of Christ, Christian Churches, Disciples. 'Restorationist' is also used for the Latter Day Saints; kept to the Stone-Campbell movement here and the LDS branch named for itself, to avoid the ambiguity.

nodes.label: Schwarzenau Brethren
nodes.note: The German Baptist Brethren line — Church of the Brethren, Old German Baptist, Dunkard, Brethren in Christ. Not to be confused with the Plymouth Brethren, who are unrelated, or with the Moravians, who call themselves Unity of the Brethren.

nodes.label: Apostolic Christian
nodes.note: The Fröhlich line, Swiss Anabaptist in origin.

nodes.label: Pietist
nodes.note: The Scandinavian free-church line — Evangelical Covenant, Evangelical Free.

nodes.label: Non-denominational
nodes.note: By construction the least satisfying node on the tree, and the second largest in the United States at 21.1M. It is a real answer people give, not a failure to classify.

nodes.label: Messianic Judaism
nodes.note: CONTESTED PLACEMENT. Filed under Christianity because the theology is Christian; adherents generally identify as Jewish, and Jewish institutions do not accept the claim. Flagged rather than settled — see review notes in usrc2020.py.

nodes.label: Other Christian
nodes.note: Bodies with no branch to belong to, not a residual. The computed residual is a different thing and is named '…, other or unspecified' — see spec.md §3.2.

nodes.label: Islam
nodes.review: Muslim Estimate -> islam. Named an estimate by ASARB itself. No internal detail, so Sunni/Shia/Ahmadi are invisible in the US on this source.

nodes.label: Unitarian Universalism
nodes.note: Christian in origin, not now in self-description. Top level rather than under Christianity for that reason.

nodes.label: Hebrew Israelite
nodes.note: CONTESTED PLACEMENT. Not a branch of Judaism, and Judaism does not recognise the claim; not straightforwardly Christian either. Own family, flagged.

nodes.label: Secular and ethical
nodes.note: Organised non-theistic bodies and stated secular positions — Ethical Culture, and Canada's Atheist / Agnostic / Humanist answers. Distinct from `unaffiliated`, which is the absence of an answer rather than a position.

nodes.label: No religion
nodes.note: People who report no religion. NOT the same quantity as the US residual, which is 'absent from every membership roll' — see spec §3.1 on the basis clash at the border. Held as a real node because Canada, Australia, NZ, Ireland and the UK all measure it directly and it is the largest single answer in several of them.

nodes.label: Pagan and nature religions
nodes.note: Wicca, Neopaganism, Druidry, nature religions. StatCan groups these explicitly; the ABS buries them inside Other Religious Groups (§3.9).

nodes.label: Chinese religions
nodes.note: Chinese folk religion, Confucianism and the syncretic practice that census categories usually cannot separate — the §3.3 combination node for China's own tradition. Daoism is a sibling top-level family rather than a child, because sources enumerate it separately where they enumerate anything at all.

nodes.label: Indigenous and traditional religions
nodes.note: Traditional religions of indigenous peoples, kept as one family with regional children rather than scattered, because sources report them that way.

nodes.label: Druze
nodes.note: Its own family. Sometimes filed under Islam by sources and by convention; the Druze themselves generally do not accept that placement, and StatCan lists it separately.

nodes.label: Nazarene Christian Congregation (Side A or B)

nodes.label: Fellowship of Evangelical Churches

nodes.label: Missionary Church
nodes.review: Missionary Church -> anabaptist.mennonite. Origin is Mennonite Brethren in Christ; present identity is broadly evangelical/holiness.
